main_body: A 64x48 farm ground patch: a speckled wheat/golden crop strip on top, a green grass-tuft band, and tilled brown soil rows with sprouts below. It is terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none: the column scan shows a speckled crop texture (rows 0-14), then a grass band (rows 16-19) and soil. This is a ground texture, not a top surface over a front face.
evidence: The kind is terrain (ground tiles), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. There is no standing volume, no receding side face and no flat elevation of a standing body. The tile is a ground-surface pattern that reads as a ground patch, so I treat it as acceptable.

style.evidence: Soil has about 5 brown steps (dark edge, deep, mid, highlight clods) and grass has 4 greens (light, mid, tufts, dark). The crop strip mixes several yellows and olives in a speckle. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark brown or green material tones, not near-black. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no flat areas. Median 13 colours per tile is above the Beodeul median of about 10 and well above the paving reference (7), though below the grass reference (26). Total distinct colours (23) is low next to the grass reference (80), and the soil rows repeat horizontally, which makes it somewhat tidy. It would sit acceptably beside the references without looking sticker-like.
